* Fix reward exploits and add all-items weapon rewards

Bomb detection: Use NES animation state transitions instead of inventory
delta, which was masked by per_frame bombs=4 replenishment.

PBRS weapon ratchet: Only compute PBRS on MOVE actions. Weapon actions
press directional buttons that shift Link's position, creating a ratchet
where weapon-induced shifts go unpenalized but corrective MOVEs get rewarded.

PBRS cross-room exploit: Seed baseline from current tile on room entry
and skip PBRS that step, preventing old-room wavefront lookups.

Universal miss penalty: All non-MOVE, non-BOMB weapon/item misses get
penalty-attack-miss regardless of enemy presence.

Boomerang stun reward with anti-farming (first stun per enemy per room).
Rebalanced bomb economics (penalty -0.50 -> -0.25, hit +0.25 -> +0.50).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Add --profile flag and TUI performance optimizations

Profiling: --profile N skips 20K warmup steps, enables cProfile for N
steps through the next model update, saves to training.prof, then exits.
Forces parallel=1 (in-process) when profiling.

TUI throttle: Add 0.5s wall-clock throttle to _refresh() in the training
display. Only the hot-path on_progress is throttled; events like scenario
changes, optimize stats, and key presses use force=True for immediate
display. Reduces TUI overhead from ~14% to negligible.

* Fix multihead action masking: condition direction mask on selected type

The [K+4] multihead mask decomposed (type, direction) constraints into
independent marginals via OR-reduction. This allowed invalid combinations
like (MOVE, N) when MOVE N was masked but SWORD N was valid — the direction
N was True because SWORD allowed it.

Changed mask format from [K+4] to [K*4] where mask[i*4+j] = True iff
action type i with direction j is valid. The model now:
1. Derives type mask as mask.view(K,4).any(dim=-1)
2. Samples/uses given action type
3. Conditions direction mask on the selected type: mask[batch, type_idx]
4. Samples direction from the type-conditioned distribution

This ensures the model can never select a direction that is invalid for
the chosen action type. The same fix applies to is_valid_action() which
now checks the joint (type, direction) entry directly.

Updated both MultiHeadAgent classes, the debugger probability display,
rollout buffer mask sizing, and all related tests. Added a new test
(test_cross_type_direction_isolation) that verifies MOVE N is forbidden
when only MOVE S and SWORD N are valid.

* Fix weapon-induced room change exploit and edge masking

Two related fixes:

1. Apply location rewards/penalties and PBRS to all actions, not just
   MOVE. Previously critique_location_change and critique_movement were
   gated behind ActionKind.MOVE in critique_gameplay. This meant a bomb
   or boomerang at a screen edge could push Link into the next room
   without incurring penalty-wrong-location, then moving back in the
   correct direction earned free reward.

   PBRS now fires on weapon actions when the tile actually changed,
   preventing the sub-tile ratchet exploit while catching tile-crossing
   weapon movements.

2. Mask all non-MOVE actions at dungeon screen edges, not just SWORD
   and BEAMS. Any directional weapon (BOMBS, BOOMERANG, etc.) at a
   screen edge presses directional buttons that can cause unintended
   room transitions.

* Add KL rollback to prevent catastrophic policy updates

When approx_kl exceeds target_kl * 4 (default: 0.08), the entire
optimization round is discarded and model weights are restored to
their pre-optimization state. This prevents the cascading failure
observed in weighted circuit training where a single bad batch
caused a 10x KL spike, destroying the value function and collapsing
progress from 14 to 0.

The rollback threshold is configurable via kl_rollback multiplier
(default 4.0x target_kl). A losses/kl_rollback metric is logged
to tensorboard for visibility.

* Remove danger tile penalty and move-to-safety reward

The danger tile penalty (-0.5) made melee engagement net-negative:
approaching an enemy cost more than hitting it rewarded (+0.25).
This incentivized camping (standing still, swinging sword repeatedly)
over actively pursuing enemies. See docs/specs/combat-engagement.md.

* Fix routing: pre-collect starting room key in Dijkstra

When the agent starts in a room with an uncollected key, the Dijkstra
pathfinder now marks that key as collected in the initial state. This
prevents equal-cost detour routes that leave and re-enter the room
just to pick up the key the agent is already standing on.

Fixes objective suggesting S/E/W from room 0x53 instead of just W.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Fix empty action mask crash: fallback to all MOVE directions

Link can reach 'impossible' tile positions via sword knockback where
can_link_move() conservatively returns False for all directions. When
combined with no enemies/items (masking SWORD), the entire action mask
becomes empty and crashes training.

Instead of raising RuntimeError, unmask all MOVE directions as a
fallback. The NES will simply not move Link if the direction is truly
blocked, and training continues without interruption.

Implement IMPALA ResNet with CoordConv and multi-head attention (#180)

* Add IMPALA ResNet with CoordConv and spatial attention pooling

New visual encoder architecture for full-screen RGB observation:

Architecture:
- ResBlock: Pre-activation residual block (ReLU→Conv→ReLU→Conv + skip)
- ImpalaResNet: 3 residual stacks (5→16→32→32) with CoordConv buffers
  and spatial self-attention pooling, producing a 256-dim feature vector
- SpatialAttentionPool: 1×1 conv Q/K/V projections, scaled dot-product
  attention over all spatial positions, weighted-sum pooling
- ImpalaCombinedExtractor: ImpalaResNet + entity attention + info = 335-dim
- ImpalaSharedAgent / ImpalaMultiHeadAgent: New Network subclasses with
  forward_with_attention() for visualization

All spatial dimensions are dynamic (works for both 168×240 cropped and
176×256 full overscan modes). CoordConv channels registered as buffers.

Observation:
- New obs_kind='full-rgb': HUD trimmed, RGB (no grayscale), no viewport
  crop, frame_stack=1. Output shape: (3, H, W) normalized [0,1].

Config:
- New model-kinds in triforce.yaml: impala-shared, impala-multihead

Debugger:
- ATTENTION overlay flag in OverlayFlags enum
- Attention heatmap checkbox in View menu
- JET colormap heatmap overlay on gameplay area
- Attention weights fetched from model via forward_with_attention()

Tests:

  ImpalaSharedAgent, ImpalaMultiHeadAgent, registration, save/load,
  both screen sizes, CoordConv buffer properties

* Fix IMPALA OOM: auto-increase minibatches for spatial attention

The 630-token spatial attention matrix (630×630 × batch) causes OOM
with the default 4 minibatches (minibatch_size=1024). Add
recommended_minibatches=16 to IMPALA agents, which PPO respects
unless explicitly overridden. This reduces minibatch size to 256,
cutting attention memory from ~1.9GB to ~0.5GB per minibatch.

* Add attention dropout to prevent attention collapse

SpatialAttentionPool now applies dropout (p=0.1) to the attention
weights during training. This prevents the model from fixating on a
single spatial position (e.g., the CoordConv corner) and encourages
it to learn content-dependent attention patterns.

Note: this changes the model architecture, so existing checkpoints
are not compatible — training must restart from scratch.

* Fix pixel-alignment bug in can_link_move_from using exact NES hotspots

coordinate offsets (tr+1 for feet). The NES computes hotspot pixel positions
directly: base_Y = ObjY + $0B, then subtracts $40 for the status bar before

- Right: col=(px+16)//8,  row=(py-53)//8
- Up:    col=px//8,        row=(py-61)//8,  checks col and col+1
- Down:  col=px//8,        row=(py-45)//8,  checks col and col+1

or despawned — e.g. tile (17,5) had distances [0, 21] in the same room.

* Revert "Fix PBRS: use exit-only wavefront for stationary potential function"

This reverts commit 7231acadecbada7498906af2ce4710b8243e9b89.

* Fix PBRS: use item-free wavefront to prevent non-stationary potential

Items dropped by killed enemies (especially respawning Zoras) shift the
wavefront when included in objectives.targets, creating a PBRS leak of
+0.25 to +1.10 per stuck room visit.

Fix: compute a separate pbrs_wavefront from pbrs_targets (all objective
targets minus items). Items still appear in the main wavefront for game
logic, but PBRS uses the stationary wavefront. This preserves the
approach-enemy signal during FIGHT while eliminating item-based drift.

Also enhances diagnose.py --infinite-pbrs with per-step item/enemy
tracking, enemy type identification, and per-room non-PBRS reward
summary for exploit diagnosis.

* Decay combat rewards per room to prevent farming respawning enemies

Zoras and similar respawning enemies provide infinite hit/beam/block
rewards since they keep surfacing. This caused the model to farm
room 0x38 instead of progressing.

Add per-room combat event tracking with exponential decay: first 8
combat events per room get full reward, then each subsequent event
is scaled by 0.5^excess. This preserves early combat signal (clearing
rooms) while making farming unprofitable.

Affected rewards: reward-hit, reward-beam-hit, reward-block-projectile.

* Add per-step time penalty for movement urgency

PBRS with γ=1 provides direction but no urgency — round trips cancel
exactly, so the agent has no reason to move quickly. This caused
progress to decline as the agent learned to farm combat in comfortable
rooms rather than push into unknown territory.

Add penalty-time (-0.01/step) alongside PBRS. Over 300 stuck steps
this costs -3.0, making farming unprofitable vs progressing. The two
signals are cleanly separated: PBRS = where to go, time penalty =
go now.

* Replace flat time penalty with escalating tile revisit penalty

PBRS with γ=1 makes oscillation free — the model learned to navigate
to within 2 tiles of the exit then bounce (28,9)↔(29,9) indefinitely.
The flat -0.01/step penalty was too weak and non-specific to break this.

Replace with tile revisit penalty (from old TILE_TIMEOUT system):
- Track visits per tile per room
- First 8 visits: free (allows healthy backtracking)
- After 8: penalty = -0.01 * visit_count (escalating: -0.09, -0.10...)
- Reset on room change, combat hits, or item gains

This specifically punishes oscillation while leaving productive
exploration and combat unpunished. Combined with PBRS for direction,
the model gets both 'where to go' and 'don't stall' signals.
